title: Thinnai
description: Raised seats along the verandah where the family once chatted with the street — and where the paati still keeps watch. Six octagonal teak pillars on granite bases carry the roof.

title: Main door & kolam
description: A carved teak double door with brass studs and ring handles. The kolam in front is drawn fresh every morning (ours is baked into the floor texture, so it never smudges).

title: Mutram
description: The open courtyard at the heart of the house: sunk a little, paved in stone, with the tulsi madam at the centre. Light, breeze and monsoon rain all arrive here.

title: Oonjal hall
description: A teak swing on brass chains, a silk cushion and cane chairs for evening coffee. Athangudi tiles underfoot, a Thanjavur-style panel on the wall.

title: Dining & kitchen
description: Red oxide floor, a teak dining table with cane chairs, and a kitchen with a black granite counter, green tiles and a shelf of brass and copper vessels. The aattukal waits in the corner.

title: Pooja niche
description: A teak-lined niche in the back wall with a gilded panel and kuthuvilakkus — on axis with the front door, so the lamps are the first thing you see.

title: Clay-tile roof
description: Mangalore tiles on teak rafters. The roof slopes out to the eaves and in to the courtyard, so the rain is collected, not wasted — and the attic stays cool.

title: Garden & well
description: Coconut trees, banana plants, jasmine by the gate and a well in the back yard with a teak pulley frame — for the house that still respects groundwater.
